chat_modes.consequence: Potential spam, inappropriate or otherwise downranked messages may not appear
Display shows messages without the Top Chat filter; channel moderation/deletion and eligibility still constrain visibility

selection_rules: Live Chat display data and available video transcripts; not Top Chat's filtered view
English language filter removes non-English chat messages, excludes streams with >70 percent non-English messages
Median inter-message interval 1 second to 5 minutes
Additional 20th–80th quantile filtering of average emotion-message rate per video
paper.model_dependency: Hawkes self-exciting process; observational with untested counterfactuals

boundaries: Self-excitation coefficients are parameters of an observational Hawkes model, not randomized causal effects or per-person emotional change.
The final 92412 coded text messages across 397 videos result from exclusions applied after the initial 673551 message / 1957-video cohort; do not add these frames.
Text-only six-category machine emotion labeling omits visuals, prosody, irony, mixed emotions beyond the six labels, and any validation of individual psychological states.
No distinction between human and automated chat accounts was verified.
Negativity lasting nearly twice as long refers to modeled emotion-expression decay, not a timed measure of lasting individual emotional harm.
Model result says nothing about revenue, moderation staffing returns, audience country, unique commenters or language-specific platform populations.

prohibited_inferences: Initial 673,551 messages across 1,957 videos and model sample 92,412 messages across 397 videos are successive selected frames, not disjoint studies or population totals.
Live Chat display is not a guarantee of retaining deleted, moderated or inaccessible posts.
Emotional language labels are algorithmic text classifications, not users' validated mental states or demographic identities.
Model-based peer versus video intensity comparisons are associational/model-dependent and do not establish experimental causality.
Sample uses English-related filters and selected message frequency; it does not represent global YouTube live chats or unique viewers.
Chat volume, chat emotion and show metadata do not provide creator revenue, paying customer conversions or online-community membership sizes.
A 0.4%–8.7% referenced-message rate from ten selected Japanese VTubers is not the platform-wide response probability or a paid-chat priority measure.
The observed 8–38 second delay applies only to manually identifiable references and excludes unaddressed chat messages.

interaction_paper.title: Discourse analysis of just-chatting streams on YouTube Live
interaction_paper.method: Manual conversational-reference alignment of first 60 minutes of 10 selected Japanese-language independent VTuber just-chatting livestreams; only author-agreed references counted; paid Super Chats excluded
interaction_paper.population: 10 intentionally chosen public Japanese-language just-chatting streams, not all Japanese VTubers or all streaming
limitations: The ten streams were purposefully selected, in Japanese, independently produced, and restricted to the first hour; fractions are per stream, not platform probabilities.
Message matching counted only matched author judgments and assigned special handling to repeated similar chat, so the unit is a methodological coding decision.
Per-stream averages of 8–38 seconds are delays for identified references, not response times for the many unaddressed messages.
Public chat messages and accounts do not reveal the number of passive viewers or identify unique people across streams.
Paid Super Chats were omitted; observed references cannot be used to estimate paid-message attention, creator income or purchase conversion.
